nonplanar triangle completion $H_1+ab+ad+bd$.
Since $H_3$ contains $H_2+bd$, Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-cut} gives
twins $p',q'$ with neighborhood $\{c,e,w\}$.
Contract the rest of $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ to $w$, retaining
only $bw,dw$ and the six edges at $p',q'$ in $B$.
The disk test and the annular choice $E_0=\{bd\}$ still fail
because they contain $H_1+ab+ad+bd$.
For $E_0=\varnothing$, the graph $H_2+bd$ has a $K_{3,3}$ minor:
the sets $\{p'\},\{q'\},\{b,d\}$ are each adjacent to $c,e,w$.
Thus minimality fixes this reduced $B$.
Keeping the triangle completion of $H_1$ nonplanar preserves
the same failures, so Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}
and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give $216$
forms. Each resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most
two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E25}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ... h1, h2 are the twins with neighbourhood {b,d,w} (p', q' in the text).

specification.exterior: Psi3 + bd + w + h1 + h2, N(w)=b,d,h1,h2, N(h1)=N(h2)=c,e,w

C + ab + ad nonplanar.meaning: B = C + ab + ad must be planar when a cross edge is present

disjoint twin triples.meaning: Section 6 assumes any two twin triples share exactly one vertex
